title: Traffic Flow Cellular Automaton with Physics Debug Overlay
prompt:
Create a single HTML file with Three.js that implements a Nagel-Schreckenberg traffic flow cellular automaton on a 2D grid, rendered in 3D with a physics debug overlay.

SCENE SETUP:
- Use an orthographic camera looking down at a 40x40 grid (top-down view, Y-up)
- Grid cells are 1x1 unit flat planes; road cells are dark gray (#333333), empty cells are green (#228B22)
- Define a road network: a main horizontal road at row 20, a main vertical road at column 20, forming a cross intersection
- Each road is 2 cells wide (rows 19-20 for horizontal, columns 19-20 for vertical)
- Place 30 vehicle agents initially distributed randomly on road cells, represented as colored box meshes (0.8x0.4x0.3 units)
- Vehicles on horizontal roads are blue (#2196F3), vehicles on vertical roads are red (#F44336)
- Add ambient light (intensity 0.6) and a directional light from above (intensity 0.8)

CELLULAR AUTOMATON RULES (Nagel-Schreckenberg):
- Each vehicle has integer speed v (0 to vmax=5 cells/step)
- Step 1: Acceleration - if v < vmax, v = v + 1
- Step 2: Slowing - if distance to next car ahead d <= v, then v = d - 1
- Step 3: Randomization - with probability p=0.3, if v > 0 then v = v - 1
- Step 4: Movement - vehicle advances v cells
- Roads wrap around (periodic boundary conditions)
- At the intersection, horizontal traffic has priority (vertical vehicles must wait if horizontal vehicle is within 3 cells of intersection)

SIMULATION CONTROLS:
- Simulation starts paused
- Press SPACE to toggle play/pause
- Press S to single-step when paused
- Press R to reset simulation to initial random state
- Press + / - to increase/decrease simulation speed (steps per second: 1, 2, 4, 8, 16)
- Press D to toggle the debug overlay

DEBUG OVERLAY:
- When enabled, render velocity vectors as arrows (ArrowHelper) on each vehicle, length proportional to speed
- Show cell occupancy as wireframe highlights (yellow wireframe on occupied cells)
- Display density heatmap: color road cells by local density (green=low, yellow=medium, red=high) calculated in a 5-cell neighborhood

HUD/UI (HTML overlay):
- Top-left: show 'Step: N', 'Vehicles: 30', 'Avg Speed: X.XX', 'Flow: X.XX veh/step'
- Top-right: show 'Speed: Xsteps/s', 'State: PAUSED/RUNNING', 'Debug: ON/OFF'
- Flow is calculated as total distance moved by all vehicles in last step divided by road length

STATE MANAGEMENT - expose window.__3D_STATE__ with:
- stepCount: integer, current simulation step number
- isRunning: boolean, whether simulation is playing
- simSpeed: number, steps per second (1,2,4,8,16)
- vehicleCount: integer (30)
- vehicles: array of {id, x, y, speed, maxSpeed, direction} for each vehicle
- avgSpeed: number, average speed of all vehicles (2 decimal places)
- flow: number, flow metric from last step
- debugEnabled: boolean
- totalDistanceMoved: number, cumulative distance all vehicles moved since start
- densityMap: object with {horizontal: number, vertical: number} representing avg density on each road
- intersectionBlocked: boolean, whether any vertical vehicle is currently waiting at intersection
- conservationValid: boolean, true if vehicleCount equals vehicles.length at all times
- lastStepDistances: array of distances each vehicle moved in the last step
- randomSeed: number, the seed used for initial placement
physics_constraints: Vehicle count must be conserved (always 30). Speeds must be integers in [0, vmax=5]. No two vehicles may occupy the same cell. Periodic boundary conditions must wrap positions correctly within [0, 39]. Flow must be non-negative. Average speed must be in [0, 5]. Intersection priority rules must prevent collisions.
